title: Indian Navy Agniveer Recruitment 2026: SSR & MR Guide
metaDescription: Indian Navy Agniveer 2026: SSR and MR entries, age 17.5-21, pay Rs 30,000-40,000, Seva Nidhi package, INET exam, eligibility and how to apply online.
headline: Indian Navy Agniveer Recruitment 2026: SSR and MR Complete Guide

sections.title: SSR and MR: Two Ways Into the Navy
sections.content:
The Indian Navy recruits Agniveers twice a year under the Agnipath scheme, in two entries. Agniveer SSR (Senior Secondary Recruit) is for candidates who have passed Class 12 with Maths and Physics, and they operate sensors, weapons and equipment on naval ships and submarines. Agniveer MR (Matric Recruit) is for Class 10 pass candidates, who serve as chefs, stewards and hygienists looking after shipboard services.

Both entries serve for four years. The 01/2027 and 02/2027 batches are being inducted through the Indian Navy Entrance Test (INET), and applications are submitted online at joinindiannavy.gov.in. Only unmarried Indian men and women are eligible, and marriage is not permitted during the four-year term.

sections.title: Age Limit and Educational Qualification
sections.content:
Candidates must be between 17.5 and 21 years old. For the 01/2027 batch, the birth window is 1 December 2004 to 31 May 2009, and for the 02/2027 batch it is 1 May 2005 to 31 October 2009, both dates inclusive. Age relaxation applies to reserved categories as per government rules.

SSR applicants need Class 12 with Maths and Physics, plus Chemistry or Biology or Computer Science as an additional subject in many notifications. MR applicants need a Class 10 pass with at least 50 percent marks overall from a board recognised by the Ministry of Education.

sections.title: Pay, Allowances and Seva Nidhi Package
sections.content:
Agniveers receive a monthly package that rises every year: Rs 30,000 in the first year, Rs 33,000 in the second, Rs 36,500 in the third and Rs 40,000 in the fourth. In-hand pay is lower because 30 percent goes into the Agniveer Corpus Fund, matched by an equal government contribution, so first-year in-hand pay is about Rs 21,000.

On completing four years, Agniveers receive a Seva Nidhi package of about Rs 10.04 lakh, including their own contribution and the matching government share. They also get risk and hardship allowances where applicable, free food, uniform, accommodation, medical cover and Rs 48 lakh non-contributory life insurance during service.

sections.title: Selection Process and Life After Four Years
sections.content:
Selection starts with a computer-based INET examination, followed by a written test, a physical fitness test and a medical examination. Shortlisted candidates are then called for final enrolment and basic training at INS Chilka, the Navy's premier training establishment, before joining ships and naval units.

Up to 25 percent of each batch can be permanently enrolled in the regular Navy cadre based on performance and organisational requirements. The rest leave after four years with the Seva Nidhi package, an Agniveer skill certificate and priority in several government and private-sector recruitment schemes.
